consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué deduce la persona sobre el hombre de la feria.

items.audio: I spoke to a man at the book fair for about ten minutes. He didn't seem nervous at all, but every time I asked him something, he gave me a one-word answer and glanced at his phone. When I mentioned the new exhibition, he said, "Sounds interesting," and that was it. I got the impression he would rather have been somewhere else.
opciones: He was too shy to say much.
He was keen to hear more about the exhibition.
He wanted the conversation to be over.

feedback.es: No parecía nervioso, contestaba con monosílabos, miraba el celular y no mostró interés real: lo que se deduce es que prefería estar en otro sitio.

consigna.es: Escucha el parte y elige el consejo principal para los excursionistas.

items.audio: Conditions on the ridge are expected to deteriorate by mid-afternoon, with gusts of up to sixty kilometres an hour and poor visibility. Thunderstorms are possible, though not certain. Anyone who hasn't reached the summit by noon had better turn back, and people caught in the open should take shelter below the ridge.
opciones: Carry on as planned, since the weather will stay fine all day.
Wait on the ridge until the storms have passed.
Head down unless they are close to the top by midday.

feedback.es: El parte dice que quien no haya llegado a la cima a mediodía haría mejor en volver; además, si hay tormenta hay que refugiarse por debajo de la cresta, no en ella.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige la condición que pone la inquilina.

items.audio: I told the landlord I'd sign for two years on the understanding that he repairs the heating before winter. He said he'd consider it, provided I paid the deposit first. I've agreed to that, but only if the repair is written into the contract. Otherwise, I'm not budging.
opciones: She will pay the deposit only if the repair is put in writing.
She will pay the deposit only once the heating has been fixed.
She will sign for two years only if the landlord lowers the deposit.

feedback.es: Acepta pagar el depósito primero, como pide el casero, pero solo si la reparación queda escrita en el contrato; no espera a que arreglen la calefacción ni negocia el depósito.

consigna.es: Escucha y decide qué concluye la persona de la respuesta de su jefa.

items.audio: When I asked my manager whether I could work from home on Fridays, she said, "That might be difficult at the moment, but I'll think about it." I've worked there long enough to know how a polite "I'll think about it" usually turns out. So I didn't push, and I haven't mentioned it since.
opciones: The manager needs a few days to make up her mind.
The request will probably not be granted.
The manager is in favour of the idea.

feedback.es: Por la cortesía indirecta («might be difficult», «I'll think about it») y por su experiencia en esa oficina, deduce que la respuesta equivale a un no.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige por qué Leo escribe «don't feel any pressure».

items.texto:
Hi Marta,
It was lovely meeting you at the book fair on Saturday. I'd really like to pick up where we left off on translation, since I've been thinking about your point regarding jargon. I'm free on Thursday evening if you fancy a coffee, but please don't feel any pressure: I realise your week may already be full. Either way, I'll send you the article I mentioned, and perhaps we could take it from there. I also enjoyed hearing about your work, and I think we have a lot in common. Hope to touch base again soon!
Best, Leo
opciones: To warn Marta that the plan for coffee may well be cancelled
To make it easy for Marta to say no without feeling awkward
To hint that Leo himself may not be free on Thursday evening

feedback.es: La frase le da a Marta una salida fácil: puede declinar sin incomodidad, porque Leo reconoce que quizá tenga la semana llena.

consigna.es: Lee el resumen del informe y elige qué postura mantienen los autores.

items.texto: Sleep and screen habits: summary of findings. A survey of 240 students in two local schools, carried out last March, found that those who used phones after ten at night reported feeling more tired at school. It appears that late screen use may contribute to poorer sleep, although there is no conclusive evidence that it is the cause. Other factors, such as homework load or early starts, were not measured. To a certain extent, then, the results only hint at a link rather than prove one, and the authors recommend a larger study before any school policy is changed.
opciones: Late phone use is probably the main cause, although this is not yet proven.
Late phone use may play a part, but the survey cannot prove it.
Other factors, such as homework, probably explain the tiredness better.

feedback.es: Usan cautela («it appears», «may contribute», «no conclusive evidence»): el móvil puede influir, pero no se prueba que sea la causa principal y otros factores ni se midieron.

consigna.es: Lee la carta al periódico y elige qué sugiere la autora sobre la medida.

items.texto: To the Editor: The council's decision to ban cycling on the riverside path was, I assume, well meant. It is hard, however, to see whom it serves. Nobody I know has ever felt unsafe there, and in five years the path has seen one minor incident. Since the ban, cyclists have simply moved onto the main road, which is much busier. Pedestrians report no real difference, and the path itself is now rather quiet. Nobody was consulted, and the council has yet to explain its reasoning. I do hope someone will think again before anyone comes to harm.
opciones: It was a sensible step that needs more time to show results.
It helps pedestrians, although cyclists have reason to be annoyed.
It does little good and may even make things less safe.

feedback.es: Concede que tal vez fue bienintencionada, pero señala que nadie gana (los peatones no notan cambio) y que los ciclistas ahora van por una calzada más peligrosa.

consigna.es: Lee el artículo y elige qué da por supuesto el argumento que critica la autora.

items.texto: Some commentators argue that remote work has made teams lazy. Admittedly, a few companies have reported slower decisions, and that deserves a closer look. Nobody denies that some managers struggle to lead from a distance. Yet the argument treats the hours people spend at a desk as if they measured effort, which is hard to defend. Most of the evidence we have so far, albeit limited, points the other way: work has held steady, and staff are more willing to volunteer for extra tasks. The question worth asking, then, is not where people work, but how we measure what they deliver.
opciones: That remote work saves companies money
That teams decide faster when they meet in person
That time spent at a desk shows how hard someone works

feedback.es: El argumento criticado equipara las horas en la oficina con el esfuerzo («as if they measured effort... hard to defend»); por eso la autora propone medir lo que se entrega.

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre el servicio del transbordador.

items.texto: In the unlikely event ___ the ferry is cancelled, all passengers will receive a full refund.

feedback.es: Tras «in the unlikely event» se usa «of» + sustantivo («of a cancellation») o «that» + oración completa: aquí sigue una oración, así que va «that».

consigna.es: Completa la disculpa con la forma verbal que encaja.

items.texto: I'm sorry. Had I listened sooner, you ___ so alone now.

feedback.es: Es un condicional mixto: la condición es pasada («Had I listened») y el resultado es presente («now»), así que va «would not feel».

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre la jornada de limpieza.

items.texto: Never before ___ so many neighbours joined the clean-up, and it is only ten o'clock.

feedback.es: Tras «Never before» se invierte el orden (auxiliar + sujeto); como el hecho llega hasta el presente, va el presente perfecto con sujeto plural: «have so many neighbours joined».

consigna.es: Elige la preposición que completa la frase.

items.texto: Owing to a shortfall ___ ticket sales, the club cancelled the final match.

feedback.es: El sustantivo «shortfall» se construye con «in» cuando nombra aquello que se queda corto: «a shortfall in ticket sales».

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que encaja en el mensaje de seguimiento.

items.texto: She hadn't replied to my message, so I sent her a gentle ___ to remind her.

feedback.es: «Nudge» es un empujoncito: un recordatorio suave para alguien que no ha respondido.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que encaja en la entrevista.

items.texto: When the panel began to ___ into my reasons for leaving, I realised they wanted more than a short answer.

feedback.es: «Delve into» es profundizar con detalle en algo; «dodge» es esquivar y «deliver» es entregar, y ninguno encaja con «into my reasons».

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que encaja en la negociación.

items.texto: Both sides were firm, and neither would ___ a single point, so the talks ended without a deal.

feedback.es: «Concede a point» es admitir que el otro tiene razón en algo; «reciprocate» es devolver un gesto y «evacuate» es desalojar.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que marca el límite de lo que aceptas.

items.texto: I'm happy to help with the garden, but I ___ at working every weekend.

feedback.es: «Draw the line at» es fijar un límite: ayudar sí, pero no trabajar todos los fines de semana.

consigna.es: Pide a tu jefa cambiar tu turno del viernes: sé cortés, da un motivo y ofrece otro día.

items.respuesta: I was wondering whether it would be possible to swap my Friday shift with someone else's. I have a medical appointment that I cannot rearrange, and I would be happy to cover a Saturday instead. Please let me know if that would be convenient.
aceptadas: Would it be possible to change my shift on Friday? I have a dentist appointment, so I cannot work that day. I could work on Saturday instead, if that would suit you.

feedback.es: Un registro formal suaviza la petición («I was wondering whether...») y ofrece una alternativa concreta.

consigna.es: Rechaza con tacto pasar la reunión al jueves: valora la idea y propón el lunes.

items.respuesta: That's a fair point, and I appreciate the suggestion. Although I see why you want to move the meeting, I'm afraid Thursday is difficult for me. Would it be possible to meet on Monday instead, provided that everyone is free?
aceptadas: Thank you for the idea, and I can see why Thursday suits you. However, it might be difficult for me that day. Could we perhaps meet on Monday instead?

feedback.es: Reconoce lo válido, matiza el rechazo («I'm afraid», «might be difficult») y ofrece una alternativa concreta.

notes: P1 gramatica.1-3: los ítems originales (may not be kept, insist that + base, Only when + inversión) eran resolubles con estructuras ya vistas en N5-N8 y, en el caso de 'insisted that ... attended', con segunda clave defendible. Sustituidos por: 'in the unlikely event that/of' (cláusula vs sustantivo), condicional mixto con inversión (Had I listened ... would not feel ... now) y 'Never before have' con trampa have/had/has/did; gramatica.4 (Should) sustituido por colocación 'shortfall in' (Should-inversión ya aparece en N10).

P1 escucha.1 y escucha.4: el audio enunciaba la conclusión ('being polite', 'nobody says no directly') y la clave era la única que repetía esa palabra; se retiró la frase explícita y las opciones parafrasean. escucha.3: distractores reescritos para que también citen deposit/heating (la clave ya no es la única que eco del audio). escucha.2: distractor 'storms very unlikely' discutible frente a 'possible, though not certain'; sustituido.

P1 lectura.3 y lectura.4: el pasaje nombraba la postura de forma explícita ('underlying assumption', riesgo 'far greater'); reescritos con tono más contenido y sin la señal léxica; se quitó 'Their worry is fair' de lectura.4 para que el distractor de decisiones lentas no sea defendible. lectura.2: opciones ahora todas con cautela graduada (probably the main cause / may play a part / probably explain).

P1 vocabulario.2-3: 'misquoted' era transparente (mis+quote) y su frase no encajaba del todo (publicar la mitad no es citar mal); 'in principle' quedaba resuelto por el contexto. Sustituidos por 'delve into' (bloque 6) y 'concede a point' (bloque 12); vocabulario.1 (nudge, bloque 1) y .4 (draw the line, bloque 20) se mantienen.

P2 escritura.1/2: grupos de evidencias ampliados con variantes naturales (could I, I've got, I need to, another day, thanks for, good idea, do not think, unfortunately...); minimoPalabras de escritura.2 baja a 25; se comprobaron 6 respuestas alumno plausibles.

Discriminación: cobertura de bloque 1 (escucha.1, lectura.1, nudge) a bloque 20 (draw the line, revisión); los ítems más accesibles son lectura.1 y escucha.2, que se dejan como entrada del nivel. Advertencia: la gramática C1 de N9 repite estructuras de N6-N8, por lo que la discriminación se apoya en trampas de tiempo/forma y no en estructuras nuevas.
